reasons: Classification is sound: Section 7 contains only a mutual consequential-damages waiver and no monetary cap anywhere, so the clause fails the fallback's material requirement of a mutual 12-month fee cap — this is not an acceptable-fallback clause being upgraded.

The redline is actionable and minimal: it leaves the existing waiver intact and adds a single new subsection with a mutual greater-of cap, the standard uncapped Excluded Claims (confidentiality/data security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), and a payment-obligations carve-out, tracking the model language.

The substitution of 'amounts paid or payable between the Parties' for 'fees paid by Customer' is a justified adaptation to the revenue-share structure (payment flows from Kubient to Customer), where a Customer-fees basis would be illusory; the USD 1,000,000 floor keeps the cap meaningful.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, states the playbook position and confirms indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap; deterministic checks all pass and no unlimited-Customer-liability language remains.
